newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland details 1997 debt servicing spending.
newsitem.headline: Finland details 1997 debt servicing spending.

text.p: The Finnish government's 1997 state budget proposal released on Tuesday gave the following details of planned state debt servicing expenditure:
Foreign currency debt interest costs (million markka):
According to the budget, the state's net debt servicing costs are forecast at 27.09 billion markka in 1997, down from 29.28 billion this year.

Finance ministry budget chief Erkki Virtanen told a news conference that the decline in debt servicing costs was due to a technical change in the budget. The comparable figure for 1997 would be 31 billion markka.

At end-997, state debt attributable to budget spending is forecast to be 416 billion markka or 69 percent of gross domestic product, up from 387 billion or 68 percent at end-1996, the budget proposal said.

Net borrowing required to cover the budget deficit would be 28.81 billion markka and total state net borrowing including other items outside the budget "was likely to be below 30 billion markka", Virtanen said.
The entire state debt including borrowing raised to cover state expenditure outside the budget would rise to 71.9 percent of GDP by end-1997 from 70.8 percent at the end of this year.
